PPNAM-SOP-001 Standard Operating Procedure Rev. B — 31 Aug 2026

Station 1 Scanner App

Operating procedure for the PPNAM Station 1 handheld RFID scanner — operator login, RFID tag assignment, pallet offloading against SAP documents, and device configuration.

System
PPNAM Station 1 AA (Android)
Device
Chainway C72 RFID handheld
App Package
com.mitas.ppnam.station1aa
App Version
v1.0 (1)
Step 1Log In Step 2Dashboard Workflow ATag Assignment Workflow BOffload
1

Overview

The Station 1 Scanner App runs on the Chainway C72 handheld and gives goods-receiving operators two workflows against the Station 1 PC:

  • Tag Assignment — register RFID pallet tags with the station. Scanning a tag sends it automatically; the station accepts or rejects each tag.
  • Offload — record each pallet coming off the truck against an SAP document (Purchase Order or Stock Transfer): scan the pallet's RFID tag and barcode, confirm the pallet values, and close the document when the delivery is complete.

Every operator signs in first — with a username and password, or by scanning their badge. What an operator can open is controlled per account: a tile the operator is not authorised for stays greyed out on the dashboard.

The scanner talks to the Station 1 PC over the site Wi-Fi using MQTT. The station validates every scan and every login. If the station goes offline, the app blocks all work with a full-screen overlay until it reconnects (Section 8).

2

Prerequisites

Confirm all of the following before starting a shift:

  • The scanner is charged and powered on.
  • Wi-Fi is connected to the site network.
  • The Station 1 PC is running and online.
  • The app is installed: com.mitas.ppnam.station1aa.
  • The handheld has been provisioned with its broker credential (one-time supervisor task — see Section 7). The connection pill in the top bar reads Connected.
  • The operator has a user account or badge registered at Station 1.
3

Logging In

Step 1

The app opens on the Log In screen. Check the connection pill at the top right reads Connected before logging in.

There are two ways to sign in:

Username + password
Type your operator username and password, then tap LOG IN. Credentials are verified by the Station 1 PC (SCRAM challenge — the password itself is never sent over the network).
Badge scan
Simply scan your badge with the RFID trigger while on the Log In screen — no typing needed.

3.1 If the Login Fails

  • Wrong password or unknown username — a red error appears under the password field. Re-type the credentials and try again.
  • Unknown badge — the same red error appears. Verify the badge is registered at Station 1.
  • No response from the station — the request times out after ~10 seconds and shows an error; the screen stays usable. Try again — if it keeps happening, check Section 8.
4

Dashboard & Operators

Step 2

After login the dashboard shows who is signed in and the two workflow tiles. Tap a tile to open that workflow; tap the back arrow inside a workflow to return here.

Operator row
Shows the signed-in operator. Tap it to log out (confirm in the dialog). Settings offers a second Log Out button.
Tag Assignment tile
Opens Workflow A (Section 5). Enabled only if your account allows it.
Offload tile
Opens Workflow B (Section 6). Enabled only if your account allows it.
⚙ / pill
The gear opens Settings; the pill shows the live broker connection (see Section 8).
Note

Always log out at the end of your shift or when handing the scanner to another operator — every scan is recorded against the signed-in operator. If the station expires your session, the app returns to the Log In screen automatically; just log in again.

5

Tag Assignment

Workflow A

Use Tag Assignment to register RFID pallet tags with Station 1. There is nothing to type — scanning is the whole workflow.

  1. On the dashboard, tap Tag Assignment.
  2. Point the scanner at the pallet tag and pull the trigger. The tag is sent automatically — no submit button.
  3. Watch the Last Scanned card: the tag ID appears with a status underneath. Green means assigned; red means rejected (see 5.1).
  4. Repeat for every tag. The card always shows the most recent scan.

5.1 Rejected or Failed Scans

A red status under the tag means the station did not accept it:

Tag already in use.
Another scanner holds this tag. Use a different tag, or have the other operator release it.
Tag unknown.
The tag is not in the station's tag pool. Set it aside and report it to your supervisor.
No response from station — try again
The station did not answer within 10 seconds. Scan the same tag again — a successful retry assigns it normally.
Tip

Re-scanning a tag you already own is harmless — the station simply confirms it as assigned again.

6

Offload

Workflow B

Use Offload as pallets come off the truck. Each pallet carries an RFID tag and a barcode label; the station checks that the two belong to the same pallet and tells you which SAP document it belongs to.

6.1 Scan & Match

  1. On the dashboard, tap Offload.
  2. Scan the pallet's RFID tag and its barcode (either order — each scan fills its own field automatically; you can also type them).
  3. Tap MATCH PALLET. The button enables once both fields are filled.

If the station rejects the pair, the reason appears in red and you stay on the scan step:

Pair mismatch.
Tag and barcode belong to different pallets — re-scan the label and tag on the same pallet.
Barcode not found
The label is not in the system. Check you scanned the pallet label, not another sticker.
Already offloaded
This pallet was recorded earlier — it does not need scanning again.
Document unknown / closed
The pallet's document is not open — see 6.4, or call your supervisor.

6.2 Confirm the Pallet Values

On a successful match, the Pallet Values card appears. The heading shows the SAP document and progress (e.g. PO-000123 · 5 of 12 pallets), and the station pre-fills the expected values.

  1. Check Bag Weight (kg), Number of Bags, and Batch Reference against what is physically on the pallet. Correct any of them if the pallet differs.
  2. Tap CONFIRM OFFLOAD. (Use BACK TO SCAN to abandon this pallet — the scanned pair is kept.)

The app blocks obviously wrong values before sending: weight and bag count must be greater than zero and the batch reference cannot be empty. If the station rejects a value, the reason shows in red and you stay on this card to fix it; if there is no response, wait for the timeout message and tap CONFIRM OFFLOAD again.

6.3 Pallet Recorded — Next Pallet or Done

On success a dialog confirms the pallet and shows the updated progress:

Next Pallet
The everyday action — clears the scan fields for the next pallet on the truck.
Done
Only when the delivery for this document is finished — opens the document-closing dialog (6.4).

6.4 Closing the Document

Tapping Done asks how to close the document. Pick the outcome that matches what was actually received — the colors mirror the meaning:

Short
Fewer pallets arrived than the document expects.
Complete
Everything expected was received.
Over
More arrived than expected.
Caution

Closing is final for this delivery: pallets belonging to a closed document can no longer be offloaded. If the close fails (station error), the dialog is offered again — just pick the outcome once more. Cancel backs out without closing.

7

Settings

Supervisor

Open Settings with the ⚙ gear in the top bar (available from the Log In screen and the dashboard). Diagnostics are visible to everyone; changing the configuration requires the supervisor PIN.

7.1 Diagnostics

MQTT Broker
This handheld's own connection to the broker — Connected is required for everything.
Station 1
Whether the Station 1 PC is online. Can be Offline even while the broker is Connected.
Version / Device ID
Quote both when reporting a problem (e.g. v1.0 (1), scanner_7f514e748f9b).
Lockout

Five wrong PINs lock the gate for 30 seconds — the correct PIN is refused during the lockout. Wait it out, then try again.

7.2 Broker Configuration & Provisioning

After unlocking with the PIN, the Broker form appears with the current settings. This is also how a new handheld is provisioned: until a broker password has been saved once, the app deliberately stays offline.

  1. Enter the Host, Port, and the Use WebSocket / Use TLS switches as instructed by IT.
  2. Enter the broker Username and Password. The password field is always shown empty — leaving it blank keeps the already-saved credential; typing a value replaces it.
  3. Tap SAVE & RESTART. The app restarts, reconnects with the new settings, and returns to the Log In screen.
Note

The broker password is stored encrypted on the device. An invalid value (e.g. port 0) is refused locally — fix the field and save again. After a factory reset or app-data wipe the credential is gone and the handheld must be provisioned again.

8

Connectivity & Offline

The pill in the top bar shows this scanner's broker connection on every screen:

Connected
Normal — all workflows available.
Connecting
The app is (re)establishing the broker connection — wait a moment.
Offline
No broker connection — check Wi-Fi; if it persists, check the broker settings (Section 7) or whether the device was ever provisioned.

8.1 Main Station Offline

If the Station 1 PC itself goes offline, the app blocks all work with a full-screen overlay (the pill reads "Station 1 offline"). Scans and logins are impossible until the station returns.

Note

The overlay clears by itself the moment Station 1 comes back online — no action is needed on the scanner. If it does not clear, confirm the Station 1 PC is running, then check this scanner's own connection (pill and Settings diagnostics).
